LD 917 - An Act Regarding Charges to Uninsured Patients For Covid-I9 Vaccines

March 20, 2025
Senator Bailey, Representative Gramlich and members of the Health Coverage, Insurance
and Financial Services Committee, I am Representative Josh Morris.
This bill repeals a provision of law adopted in 2021 that prohibits providers from seeking
reimbursement for COVID-19 vaccinations administered to the uninsured. Whatever logic may have existed for this policy in 2021 no longer exists today.
At the time, much of the vaccine material supplied to Maine providers was free of charge.
While there are costs beyond just the material --for example, staff time to administer the vaccine, paperwork etc. -- I was comfortable supporting this provision in 2021. Although, I will say I did propose sun setting this provision as well as others. Vaccine material is no longer supplied for free and there is no longer a worldwide pandemic of COVID-19.
As such, it is past time that we remove a state law mandating that healthcare
professionals give away their services for free. We should be reasonable with the use of
our power and repeal this law to help our providers.
I ask for your support for this legislation. I am happy to answer any questions you may
have.

Joshua Morris State Representative

In 2021 the legislature passed LD 1 An Act To Establish the COVID-19 Patient Bill of
Rights and To Amend the Governor's Emergency Powers. In negotiating this bill
agreement was reached to prohibit charges for COVID-19 vaccination for uninsured patients. The expectation was that the federal government would provide COVID-19 vaccine to states as they do other vaccines, like the flu vaccine. States then distribute the vaccines for public health administration. This is what happened for the first few years when the COVID-19 vaccine became available. On September 3, 2024 the Federal Bridge program that covered the cost of COVID vaccinations for uninsured patients ended. State law in Maine prohibits pharmacies or healthcare providers from charging the patient for expenses related to COVID vaccination.

Both the Maine Adult and Pediatric Immunization Programs as well as Maine Public Health Departments can provide COVID vaccines to uninsured patients without retail pharmacies and non-participating health centers incurring the cost. it is our understanding that the state has a very limited number of COVID-19 vaccine doses for this purpose. The reality is without federal distribution of the vaccine, clinicians and pharmacists providing the vaccine must purchase the vaccine to administer to patients or to the public. For Northern Light Health the vaccine costs approximately $98 per
dose.

Patients with our primary care clinicians receive the vaccine at the care location and our charity ca re policies apply. For the public access to the vaccine at our pharmacy
locations in Bangor, Brewer, Waterville and Ellsworth. At these locations we bill for the
vaccine and administration to private insurers, individuals can also choose to pay
privately. But if the individual is uninsured, we do not provide the vaccine as the law prohibits our ability to charge them for this service.
